title: Laurent coaction on sections of a linearized line over a ring
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $r\geq0$, and $C=A[t_1^{\pm1},\ldots,t_r^{\pm1}]$. Write $T=\operatorname{Spec}C=\mathbf G_{m,S}^r$, where $C$ has $A$-basis $t^u$ for $u\in\mathbf Z^r$, $t^ut^v=t^{u+v}$, $\Delta(t^u)=t^u\otimes t^u$, $\varepsilon(t^u)=1$, and antipode $t^u\mapsto t^{-u}$. Let $f:X	o S$ be a separated finite-type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let $a:T	imes_S X	o X$ be an $S$-action satisfying the unit and associativity identities [def-pc-fibre-product], and let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] with a $T$-linearization. A $T$-linearization of an invertible module $M$ means an isomorphism $	heta:p_2^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}a^*M$ on $T	imes_S X$ [def-pc-module-pullback], restricting to $1_M$ along the identity and satisfying $	heta_{gh,x}=	heta_{g,hx}	heta_{h,x}$ on $T	imes_S T	imes_S X$ as an equality of pulled-back sheaf maps. Put $V=\Gamma(X,L)$. There is an $A$-linear map $c:V	o V\otimes_A C$ with $(c\otimes1)c=(1\otimes\Delta)c$ and $(1\otimes\varepsilon)c=1_V$. Its normalization is the following: for every commutative $A$-algebra $B$ and $g\in T(B)=(B^	imes)^r$, the pullback to $X_B=X	imes_S\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $(1\otimes\operatorname{ev}_g)c(s)$ is the section $g\cdot s_B$ given by $(g\cdot s_B)(x)=	heta_{g,g^{-1}x}(s_B(g^{-1}x))$; here $\operatorname{ev}_g(t^u)=\prod_
u g_
u^{u_
u}$, and the notation means equality of sections via pullback along the automorphism $x\mapsto g^{-1}x$, not merely equality at geometric points. If $c(s)=s\otimes t^u$, this gives $g\cdot s_B=\operatorname{ev}_g(t^u)s_B$ for every $B$. No normality, Noetherianity, properness, finite generation of $V$, or flatness of $B$ is assumed. In particular no assertion that $V\otimes_A B	o\Gamma(X_B,L_B)$ is an isomorphism for nonflat $B$ is included.

The normalized section coaction is an agent-formulated consequence of that base-change map and the explicit linearization identity and cocycle, not a verbatim assertion of 02KH.

proof.text: The morphism $f$ is quasi-compact by the definition of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and is quasi-separated by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. The module $L$ is quasi-coherent by [def-sc-invertible-module]. For $R=C$ and $R=D=C\otimes_A C$, the displayed Laurent bases give $R\cong\bigoplus_I A$ as $A$-modules (with $I=\mathbf Z^r$ or $I=\mathbf Z^r\times\mathbf Z^r$). Consequently $N\otimes_A R\cong\bigoplus_I N$; tensoring an injection with $R$ remains injective, component by component. Thus $A\to R$ is flat by [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and $\operatorname{Spec}R\to S$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine]. These verify all hypotheses of degree-zero flat base change, without a finiteness condition on the section module.

proof.text: For every $A$-algebra $B$ define $\beta_B:V\otimes_A B\to\Gamma(X_B,L_B)$ by $s\otimes b\mapsto b\,p_B^*s$, using the pullback unit of [def-pc-module-pullback]. For $B=C,D$ this is the degree-zero canonical base-change map, hence is an isomorphism by [lem-pc-flat-base-change-cohom]. For a map $\varphi:B\to B'$ let $j:X_{B'}\to X_B$ be the induced morphism [def-pc-fibre-product]. Directly on a pure tensor, $j^*\beta_B(s\otimes b)=\varphi(b)p_{B'}^*s=\beta_{B'}(s\otimes\varphi(b))$. Additivity proves this equality on every tensor. This naturality uses no flatness of $B'$ and makes no assertion that $\beta_{B'}$ is invertible.

source.place: Tag 02KH, lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology, degree zero; agent construction from the displayed action, linearization unit and cocycle in this item.

proof.text: Put $Y=T\times_S X$, $p:Y\to X$, and $q=a\circ(i\times1):Y\to X$, so $q(g,x)=g^{-1}x$. The morphism $b:Y\to Y$, $b(g,x)=(g,g^{-1}x)$, is obtained by the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]; the action identities give $a\circ b=p$ and $p\circ b=q$ as scheme maps. Pullback of $\theta$ therefore gives an isomorphism $\lambda=b^*\theta:q^*L\to p^*L$, using composition of pullbacks [def-pc-module-pullback]. Define $K(s)=\lambda(q^*s)\in\Gamma(Y,p^*L)$ and $c(s)=\beta_C^{-1}K(s)$, identifying $Y=X_C$ by exchanging factors. Both pullback of sections and $\lambda$ respect the $A$-action, since all morphisms are over $S$; hence $c$ is $A$-linear.

proof.text:
For $g\in T(B)$, the morphism $j_g:X_B	o Y$ is $(g,p_B)$. Its coordinate map on $C$ is $\operatorname{ev}_g$, since $t^u\mapsto\prod_
u g_
u^{u_
u}$. Pulling back $ eta_C(c(s))=K(s)$ and using Step 2 gives $ eta_B((1\otimes\operatorname{ev}_g)c(s))=j_g^*K(s)$. The identities $qj_g=p_B\circ\alpha_{g^{-1}}$ and $bj_g=(g,p_B\circ\alpha_{g^{-1}})$ show that the right hand side is $	heta_{g,g^{-1}x}(s_B(g^{-1}x))$, namely $g\cdot s_B$. Here $\alpha_{g^{-1}}:X_B	o X_B$ is the inverse action automorphism. These are identities of pullback sheaf maps and their sections by [def-pc-module-pullback], so the formula holds over arbitrary $B$, including nonreduced and nonflat algebras.

source.place: Tag 02KH, lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology, degree zero; agent construction from the displayed action, linearization unit and cocycle in this item.

proof.text: Over any $A$-algebra $B$, apply the same pullback-sheaf formula to an arbitrary section $v$ of $L_B$. For $g,h\in T(B)$ the composite $g\cdot(h\cdot v)$ has, in pullback notation, the expression $\theta_{g,g^{-1}x}\theta_{h,h^{-1}g^{-1}x}v(h^{-1}g^{-1}x)$. Pull back the stated cocycle $\theta_{gh,y}=\theta_{g,hy}\theta_{h,y}$ along $y=h^{-1}g^{-1}x$. Since $hy=g^{-1}x$ and $(gh)^{-1}x=h^{-1}g^{-1}x$, this expression equals $(gh)\cdot v$. The unit identity similarly gives $1\cdot v=v$. Composition of these pulled-back maps is justified by [def-pc-module-pullback]. Each operator is $B$-linear because the action automorphisms are over $\operatorname{Spec}B$ and the linearization is a module-sheaf isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 02KH, lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology, degree zero; agent construction from the displayed action, linearization unit and cocycle in this item.

proof.text: Take $B=D=C\otimes_A C$ and the two universal points $g,h\in T(D)$ corresponding to $t^u\mapsto t^u\otimes1$ and $t^u\mapsto1\otimes t^u$. Write the finite sums $c(s)=\sum_i s_i\otimes f_i$ and $c(s_i)=\sum_j s_{ij}\otimes f_{ij}$. By Step 4 and the $D$-linearity in Step 5, $g\cdot(h\cdot s_D)=\sum_{i,j} f_{ij}(g)f_i(h)(s_{ij})_D$, which is exactly $\beta_D((c\otimes1)c(s))$. Step 4 for $gh$ gives $(gh)\cdot s_D=\beta_D((1\otimes\Delta)c(s))$, since evaluation at $gh$ is $\Delta:C\to D$ on every Laurent monomial. Step 5 equates these sections. The injectivity of $\beta_D$ from [lem-pc-flat-base-change-cohom] proves $(c\otimes1)c=(1\otimes\Delta)c$. This tests equality at the universal pair over $D$, with an injective section comparison, rather than at geometric points.

source.place: Tag 02KH, lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology, degree zero; agent construction from the displayed action, linearization unit and cocycle in this item.

proof.text: In Step 4 take $B=A$ and the identity point, whose evaluation is $\varepsilon$. Since $\beta_A:V\otimes_A A\to V$ is the canonical identification and $1\cdot s=s$ by Step 5, one gets $(1\otimes\varepsilon)c(s)=s$. Finally if $c(s)=s\otimes t^u$, the formula of Step 4 reads $g\cdot s_B=\operatorname{ev}_g(t^u)s_B$. The only inverse section comparisons used were $\beta_C$ and $\beta_D$, both flat cases; all other specializations were pullbacks of an already constructed section.
